operator_instruction.text: 完整 GPU 希望至少運作 24HR 的量，你盡量安排，直到我們能找到 eval model 在哪個臨界點失靈

launch_authorization.scope: apply 52 signal-level single-variable interventions (23 should-tie, 30 should-lose ladders incl. clean ref) to 5,131 MusicCaps-shared clips of 5 systems (real, ours CFG3+neg, ours CFG0, MusicGen, MusicLDM; 115 lvl30 audio), score AES + MEva + CLAP(batch 1) + VGGish; per-pair win/tie/lose analysis. No generation, no training.

question: For each metric, at what magnitude does a should-tie change (gain, polarity, format, lead silence, MP3) stop being judged a tie, and at what magnitude does an obvious degradation (noise, clipping, bitcrush, clicks, dropout, lowpass, blasts, shuffle, reverse) start being judged worse, pair by pair?

fixed_protocol.variants: see VARIANTS in action; transforms at native sr, output clipped to +-0.999 with over-FS count recorded, per-clip RNG crc32(system/variant/id)
fixed_protocol.judgment: delta = score(variant) - score(clean); tie if |delta| <= m, m = 0.10 S, S = range of the 5 systems' clean means per metric; pass = 80% of pairs; full m curve 0..0.5 S reported
fixed_protocol.fad: VGGish per unit (mu, sigma); FAD vs own clean and vs real clean
fixed_protocol.reading: no human ratings; MEva and CLAP read alongside AES; PC has no directed expectation

resume.note: unit-level restart (variant x system): a unit with matching ids, done.json and fad_stats is skipped; a partial one is redone whole

completion_evidence.method: guest writes terminal with sha256 of the registered summary after --validate-only passes
